title: F-Divergences, Rényi Information, and Hypothesis Testing

items.title: Finite probability vectors
proof_obligations: Specify the finite nonempty alphabet, nonnegative coordinates, normalization, and zero coordinates.

items.title: Finite stochastic kernels
proof_obligations: Fix the input/output alphabets and the row-stochastic convention.
Define the induced output law with the input-first kernel convention.

items.title: Finite f-divergence with support conventions
proof_obligations: State the convex generator class and both boundary limits.
Define zero and singular-support contributions without an ambiguous 0 times infinity.

items.title: Finite type-II testing function with explicit orientation
proof_obligations: Fix P as the null and Q as the alternative.
Define the rejection function, type-I constraint, and type-II objective; show the infimum is a real number.

items.title: Finite Kullback–Leibler divergence
proof_obligations: State the natural-log convention and the p-positive/q-zero infinity branch.
Identify KL with the f-divergence generated by t log t.

items.title: The closed convex perspective is subadditive
proof_obligations: Define the perspective at (0,0), on the positive b-axis, and on the singular boundary b=0.
Prove the finite-sum inequality for both positive total second coordinate and total second coordinate zero.

items.title: Finite Rényi divergence
proof_obligations: State the order range, the order-one value, and support/zero conventions for orders below and above one.
Define the zero-affinity case as extended value +infinity.

items.title: Finite iid log-likelihood averages concentrate
proof_obligations: Assume P is absolutely continuous with respect to Q on the finite alphabet.
Use boundedness on supp(P), independence, variance additivity, and Chebyshev's inequality.

items.title: Finite data processing for f-divergences
proof_obligations: Apply perspective subadditivity at each output symbol.
Use positive homogeneity and the row-sum-one kernel identity.
Retain singular support terms.

items.title: Finite data processing for Kullback–Leibler divergence
proof_obligations: Use the t log t generator and check its recession term at infinity.
Show the f-divergence specialization is exactly the stated KL convention.

items.title: Finite data processing for Rényi divergence
proof_obligations: Treat 0<alpha<1 and alpha>1 separately because division by alpha−1 reverses order below one.
Use the convex generators 1−t^alpha and t^alpha−1 respectively.
Handle infinite divergences and zero affinity explicitly.

items.title: The finite Rényi divergence limit is KL
proof_obligations: Handle P not absolutely continuous with respect to Q on both sides of order one.
For P absolutely continuous with respect to Q, differentiate the finite positive-support sum at one.

items.title: KL is the iid type-II testing exponent
proof_obligations: For P not absolutely continuous with respect to Q, construct an eventually feasible zero-type-II test.
For P absolutely continuous with respect to Q, prove both exponent bounds using the explicit likelihood ratio.
Use the named testing orientation P=null, Q=alternative and epsilon as the type-I upper bound.

title: F-Divergences, Rényi Information, and Hypothesis Testing — Examples

items.title: Binary f-, KL-, and Rényi divergences
proof_obligations: Compute KL, order-1/2 and order-2 Rényi values for the stated binary laws.
Check the total-variation generator with the repository's one-half normalization.

items.title: Disjoint supports and singular divergence values
proof_obligations: Evaluate zero-support terms for total variation, KL, and all positive Rényi orders.
Explain why no 0 times infinity contribution is introduced.

items.title: A binary Neyman–Pearson boundary randomization
proof_obligations: Specify null and alternative orientation and the type-I/type-II conventions.
Verify exact boundary randomization and prove the finite optimization directly.
Show the likelihood-ratio threshold uses Q/P, consistent with rejecting the null P in favor of Q.
